issues.title: ESE Prelims 2021 · Q54
issues.issue: The printed emf law gives an indicated temperature of 100[E(30)−E(0)]/[E(100)−E(0)]=30.3559°C. None of the four printed options matches; excluded from automatic scores pending an authoritative correction.
issues.referenceAnswer: The printed emf law gives an indicated temperature of 100[E(30)−E(0)]/[E(100)−E(0)]=30.3559°C. None of the four printed options matches; excluded from automatic scores pending an authoritative correction.

issues.title: GATE XE 2008 · Set1 · Q23
issues.issue: Inconsistent fixed-mass ideal-gas endpoint data; the doubled-volume condition contradicts the stated final pressure and temperature.
issues.referenceAnswer: The source states that volume doubles while p falls500→100 kPa andT falls370→300 K. For a fixed ideal-gas mass, pV/T must stay constant; those endpoints do not satisfy it. No unique maximum work can be obtained without correcting the data.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2023 · Q31
issues.issue: The supplied question has no uniquely supported listed answer.
issues.referenceAnswer: The speed ratio gives nozzle exit speed 144/0.48=300 m/s, so its actual enthalpy drop from rest is 300²/2000=45 kJ/kg. An isentropic heat drop additionally requires nozzle efficiency, which is not supplied. Blade velocity coefficient cannot substitute for nozzle efficiency.

issues.title: GATE XE 2008 · Set1 · Q29
issues.issue: Exit pressure0.1MPa contradicts the1.5bar property table supplied with the question.
issues.referenceAnswer: h2=2756.7+(50²−600²)/2000=2577.95 kJ/kg. Using the supplied1.5 bar table givesx≈0.948(optionD), but the stem says exit0.1 MPa, whose correct saturation data give a different quality.

issues.title: GATE XE 2013 · Set1 · Q12
issues.issue: The source does not require reversibility; its first/second-law conditions permit a range of temperatures, with maximum400K.
issues.referenceAnswer: Energy balance gives2 kJ rejected. Entropy inequality1/600+1/300−2/T≤0 gives0<T≤400 K. The limiting reversible value is400 K, but the printed conditions alone do not select a unique temperature.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2025 · Q58
issues.issue: The generally correct combination is not among the supplied alternatives.
issues.referenceAnswer: Carnot requires reversible processes, so statement 2 is false. Statement 1 explains a practical limitation. A perfect gas with constant specific heat is not a necessary Carnot-cycle condition, so statement 3 is not generally true. The only generally correct statement is 1, absent from the options.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2018 · Q13
issues.issue: The supplied answer table marks this exercise with an asterisk; no reliable unique option is supplied.
issues.referenceAnswer: The supplied solved-book answer table on PDF page196 gives * for Q3.114.

issues.title: GATE ME 1994 | Thermodynamics Book Q3.7
issues.issue: The printed key leaves the heater entropy blank/asterisked; its thermodynamic state is not specified.
issues.referenceAnswer: Water entropy change=20×4186ln(353.15/303.15)≈12781.72J/K (the book uses roundedKelvin values and prints12786.99). Entropy change of the heater requires its state/mass or an explicit reservoir model. Electrical energy carries no entropy, so a steady heater cannot simply be assigned the negative water entropy.

issues.title: GATE XE 2008 · Set1 · Q16
issues.issue: The supplied thermodynamic data give h≈1994.2kJ/kg with x≈0.766, but no option gives both values consistently.
issues.referenceAnswer: Isentropic exhaustx=(6.5422−0.4763)/(8.3960−0.4763)=0.76593; h≈1994.42 kJ/kgusing the supplied data; the closest combined choice isD (0.77, 2004.12).

issues.title: GATE XE 2008 · Set1 · Q26
issues.issue: The formula choices contain a printed exponent error; a reliable unique automatic choice is not assigned.
issues.referenceAnswer: Ideal Brayton maximum-work pressure ratio is (Tmax/Tmin)^[γ/(2(γ−1))]. The supplied scan instead prints γ/(2γ−1) in optionB, so no printed option exactly matches.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2025 · Q55
issues.issue: The wording claims that every complete cycle necessarily has nonzero net work. The first law requires Qnet=Wnet, which may both be zero. Statements 1 and 2 hold, but statement 3 needs a qualification; no unique unambiguous key is assigned.
